item.title: A Canadian BMW Dealer Drove An iX3 1,011 km On One Charge
item.dc:creator: Horatiu Boeriu
item.description:
A BMW dealership in Ontario has covered 1,011 km (628 miles) on a single charge in a 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive. Geoff Hills of Performance BMW in St. Catharines drove every one of those...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
A BMW dealership in Ontario has covered 1,011 km (628 miles) on a single charge in a 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive. Geoff Hills of Performance BMW in St. Catharines drove every one of those kilometers himself, from Niagara Falls to a little past Québec City, in just under 15 hours.

The car was the dealership’s launch unit of the NA5 iX3. Hills says the team watched BMW’s own 1,000 km drive and decided to try it themselves once their first car arrived. They finished 3.3 km ahead of BMW’s run from Hungary to Munich, on bigger wheels and with one person behind the wheel the entire way.

How Performance BMW Got 1,011 km Out Of One Charge

This was a hypermiling run, and Hills is upfront about it. The iX3 stayed in Max Range mode the whole way, with the climate control off, the windows up and the radio off. He calls it “a deliberate max range test” and says it isn’t typical of the range an owner should expect.

One thing worked against them. Performance BMW’s iX3 rode on 21-inch wheels, while BMW’s engineers fitted the smaller 20-inch wheels for their run. BMW’s EPA figures show what that costs: on 20-inch summer tires, the iX3 50 xDrive is rated at 434 miles (698 km), while the 21-inch summer and all-season setups drop to 398 and 399 miles, or about 640 km.

Over just under 15 hours, the iX3 averaged 10.8 kWh/100 km, which works out to about 5.8 miles per kWh. Covering 1,011 km in that time means an average speed of roughly 68 km/h (42 mph), so this was a long, patient day. For comparison, BMW China’s 805 km loop around Qinghai Lake in the long-wheelbase iX3 averaged 12.6 kWh/100 km.

Hills was the only person to drive the iX3. Performance BMW ran a chase car and brought a videographer along, but there were no driver swaps. Fifteen hours alone in a cabin with no heat, no air conditioning and no music is its own kind of endurance test.

How Does This Compare To BMW’s Own 1,000 km Runs?

BMW’s European run started at the Debrecen plant in Hungary, where the iX3 is built, and ended at BMW Welt in Munich after 1,007.7 km (626.1 miles), with 2% charge left. A six-person BMW development team handled the drive, avoided highways, skipped the HVAC and ran the car on 20-inch wheels. BMW said at the time that no electric BMW SAV had gone farther on a single charge.

Performance BMW’s 1,011 km tops that, but it isn’t the longest single-charge iX3 drive. In August, BMW China drove an iX3 50L xDrive, the long-wheelbase version built for China, 1,030.2 km (640 miles) from its Shenyang plant to its R&D center in Beijing and still had 5% left. That car uses the same 108.7-kWh battery as the standard iX3.

What Range Should iX3 Owners In Canada Actually Expect?

Natural Resources Canada certifies the 2027 iX3 50 xDrive at up to 698 km on the same test cycle the EPA uses, up from the 650 km BMW Canada had estimated before certification. That number applies to the most efficient wheel and tire setup. On 21s, the EPA figures put it closer to 640 km. Canadian pricing starts at $75,900 CAD.

Nobody is driving to Québec City in January with the heat off, so treat 1,011 km as a ceiling rather than a forecast. Speed, temperature, terrain and cabin heating all pull real-world range below what Hills managed.

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com

item.title: 2027 BMW X5 50e, M60e, iX5 60 Configurators Go Live In Europe
item.dc:creator: Adrian Padeanu
item.description:
BMW is giving customers more ways to configure its latest X5, with three electrified versions of the luxury SUV now available to build online. The German automaker has opened the configurators for the X5 50e...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
BMW is giving customers more ways to configure its latest X5, with three electrified versions of the luxury SUV now available to build online. The German automaker has opened the configurators for the X5 50e xDrive, X5 M60e xDrive, and fully electric iX5 60 xDrive, expanding a lineup that already includes gasoline and diesel powertrains.

Although we’re using German pricing for this article, you can configure all three X5s in other European markets, with local prices and equipment varying by country.

The X5 50e xDrive Starts at €102,800

The entry point to the newly added plug-in hybrids is the X5 50e xDrive, which starts at €102,800 in Germany. It pairs a turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six gasoline engine with an electric motor to produce 482 horsepower and 700 Nm (516 lb-ft) of torque. BMW quotes an electric-only range of up to 102 kilometers (63 miles) on the WLTP cycle.

With a 29-kWh battery pack, the 50e should appeal to customers who want to cover their daily commute on electricity while keeping the flexibility of a gasoline engine for longer journeys.

BMW X5 M60e xDrive Costs From €125,000

At the other end of the plug-in hybrid spectrum sits the X5 M60e xDrive, starting at a hefty €125,000 in Germany. Its electrified powertrain delivers a combined 604 hp and 800 Nm (590 lb-ft) of torque, making it the more performance-focused choice for buyers who aren’t ready to go fully electric.

It uses the same battery as the 50e xDrive, but its performance focus comes at the expense of some efficiency, with the electric range dropping to 98 kilometers (61 miles). The M60e combines the everyday usability of a luxury SUV with the added punch of an electrified powertrain. Still, its six-figure starting price leaves little room for restraint when browsing the options list.

BMW iX5 60 xDrive Also Starts at €125,000


Interestingly, the all-electric iX5 60 xDrive starts at the same €125,000 as the M Performance plug-in hybrid. It marks the first fully electric X5 and uses BMW’s sixth-generation eDrive technology, with new cylindrical cells for the enormous 141-kWh battery pack.

Range is one of its headline figures. BMW lists a preliminary WLTP range of up to 845 kilometers (525 miles). The iX5 also supports DC fast charging up to 460 kW, potentially making charging stops much shorter at a sufficiently powerful station.

Like the other X5 variants, BMW will build the electric SUV at its Spartanburg plant in South Carolina, making it the first fully electric BMW produced at the U.S. factory.

  • 2027 BMW iX5 In Matte Blue Unwrapped At Athens Auto Show

    The fifth-generation X5 has made its Greek debut at the 2026 Athens Auto Show, and BMW is using the opportunity to show off the el...

  • 2027 BMW X5 Goes Meaner With M Performance Parts

    BMW wastes no time giving new X5 owners more ways to personalize their luxury SUVs. The original SUV from Bavaria can be ordered w...

More Ways to Buy A New BMW X5

The arrival of three electrified variants adds choice to the fifth-generation X5 lineup. For a few weeks already, customers have been able to configure the conventionally powered 40 xDrive and 40d xDrive.

BMW isn’t finished, either. A V8-powered X5 M60 xDrive is expected to join the European lineup later in 2027, giving buyers another option if they prefer a traditional combustion engine over the electrified alternatives.

We wouldn’t rule out further expansion, either, with a more affordable iX5 and a pricier M Performance iX5 both possibilities, although BMW hasn’t announced either model. Another educated guess is a new-generation X5 M, which we’ve heard could have a split personality, offering both V8 power and a fully electric alternative. Let’s not forget the hydrogen fuel-cell version, due later this decade, which could wear an iX5 60H xDrive badge.

For now, the expanded configurator reinforces BMW’s Power of Choice strategy. Whether you want a six-cylinder gasoline engine, a diesel, a plug-in hybrid, or a fully electric powertrain, the X5 family is preparing to offer something for just about every premium-SUV buyer. The only real question is how many options you’ll add before that already hefty starting price climbs even higher.

item.title: The 2027 BMW iX4 M60 Brings 603 hp And Matte Frozen Pure Red Paint To The Athens Auto Show
item.dc:creator: Horatiu Boeriu
item.description:
The 2027 BMW iX4 M60 xDrive made its show debut at AUTO ATHINA 2026 this week. The Bavarians pulled the covers off the 603-hp (450 kW) coupe-SUV on its stand in matte BMW Individual Frozen...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
The 2027 BMW iX4 M60 xDrive made its show debut at AUTO ATHINA 2026 this week. The Bavarians pulled the covers off the 603-hp (450 kW) coupe-SUV on its stand in matte BMW Individual Frozen Pure Red, making Athens the first place the public has seen it in the metal.

For now, the M60 tops the iX4 range. Its two motors make 875 Nm (645 lb-ft) and get it from 0-100 km/h (0-62 mph) in 3.9 seconds, a full second quicker than the iX4 50 xDrive, on the way to a 240 km/h (149 mph) top speed. The F98 X4 M Competition, the last full M version of BMW’s coupe-SUV, made 503 hp, so its electric successor beats it by 100 hp without wearing a full M badge.

BMW Skipped Paris And Gave Athens The iX4 Instead

BMW confirmed in January that it would attend the Paris Motor Show alongside MINI, then pulled out, which is how Athens ended up with the reveal. AUTO ATHINA runs from October 3 to 11 at the Metropolitan Expo, with BMW in Hall 3, Stand C1. The iX4 shares the stand with an iX5 60 xDrive in Individual Frozen Tanzanite Blue, the new i3 50 xDrive, and the facelifted 7 Series.

World premieres rarely land in Greece, and BMW brought the version of the iX4 most likely to stop foot traffic. The car also fills the gap left by the G02 X4, which ended production in 2025 without a gas-powered successor.

Frozen Pure Red And Yellow Lights Set The M60 Apart

Frozen Pure Red is one of the new iX4 colors and the shade BMW chose for the M60’s official photos, and it’s a stunning choice. Below the beltline, the iX4 is essentially an iX3. It matches its sibling in length, wheelbase, and width, and shares its bumpers and side skirts. The difference is the roof, which slopes down to a small spoiler on the decklid instead of the roof-edge spoiler the old X4 used. Every iX4 comes with the M Sport package as standard.

The M60 adds optional M Yellow Lights with three light elements that echo the stripes of the M logo, and the Iconic Glow illuminated grille is on the options list too.

More Power, Only Slightly Less Range Than The iX4 50

The M60 pairs a new synchronous motor at the rear axle with the same asynchronous front motor used in the lesser iX4s. It keeps the 108.7-kWh (net) battery from the iX4 50 xDrive, and BMW quotes up to 777 km (483 miles) of WLTP range on efficiency-focused tires. That’s only 51 km less than the iX4 50 despite 140 hp more, and 23 km more than the iX3 M60, so the sleeker roofline pays off in range as well as looks.

BMW also fits an electronically controlled M Sport rear differential, adaptive M suspension with its own spring and damper tuning, retuned variable-ratio steering, and M Sport brakes. Wheels are 21 inches as standard, with 22s and factory sport tires optional. Inside, the M60 can be ordered with M Sport seats that add massage and illuminated logos, alongside the Panoramic iDrive setup with its 17.9-inch central touchscreen.

How Much Will The iX4 M60 Cost, And When Does It Arrive?

BMW hasn’t priced the M60 yet. The iX4 40 xDrive and 50 xDrive launch in March 2027, starting at €70,900 and €75,900 in Germany. In the US, the iX4 50 xDrive starts at $66,200 before destination, with the M60 following later in 2027. Every iX4 will be built in Debrecen, Hungary, on the same line as the iX3.

The M60 also isn’t the last word on the iX4: a full X4 M electric is expected to borrow the quad-motor hardware from the electric M3. The one number BMW still hasn’t published is cargo space, and on a car whose roofline is the entire sales pitch, that’s the figure we’d want before signing anything.

item.title: By the Numbers: Can the BMW M240i Match the E46 M3?
item.dc:creator: Steven Paul
item.description:
Two measly horsepower. That’s all that separates the U.S.-spec E46 M3 from the F22 BMW M240i. One is among the most celebrated cars BMW M ever built; the other sits a rung below the full-fledged...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
Two measly horsepower. That’s all that separates the U.S.-spec E46 M3 from the F22 BMW M240i. One is among the most celebrated cars BMW M ever built; the other sits a rung below the full-fledged M cars. Both put an inline-six up front, send power to the rear wheels, and give the driver three pedals. Does the newer M240i make the M3’s reputation look a little overblown? Or does the E46 offer something its younger challenger can’t quite replicate?

Very Different Engines

The E46 M3’s naturally aspirated S54 produces 333 horsepower and 262 pound-feet of torque. Those numbers come with an important qualifier: peak horsepower arrives at 7,900 rpm, just shy of the engine’s 8,000-rpm limit. Peak torque comes at 4,900 rpm. BMW built an engine that rewards you for exploring the upper reaches of the tachometer. That’s a big part of the appeal, but it also means accessing its best requires some commitment.

The M240i takes a different approach. Its turbocharged B58 delivers 335 horsepower at 5,500 rpm, with 369 pound-feet available from 1,520 through 4,500 rpm. That’s 107 additional pound-feet—a roughly 41 percent advantage—available much earlier. In everyday driving, the numbers favor the M240i’s ability to accelerate without first reaching for a lower gear. The M3 asks you to work for its performance; the M240i makes more of it readily accessible.

Weighing In

Despite wearing the smaller model designation, the M240i doesn’t have the weight advantage. BMW lists the 2002 M3 coupe at 3,415 pounds, while its specifications for the 2018 manual M240i put that car at 3,499 pounds. Using those published figures, the newer coupe carries an additional 84 pounds. That gives the M3 approximately 0.0975 horsepower per pound, compared with the M240i’s 0.0957. It’s a small advantage, but an interesting one: the M240i’s two extra horsepower don’t entirely compensate for its additional mass.

Nevertheless, BMW quotes a quicker sprint for the newer car. The manual M240i reaches 60 mph in 4.6 seconds, compared with 4.8 seconds for the manual E46 M3. These manufacturer claims illustrate how closely the M Performance car approaches—and, in this measure, exceeds—the older M3.

Beyond the Numbers

The M3’s case extends beyond its S54 engine’s output. Its six individual throttle bodies, incredibly communicative steering, and simpler cabin layout make driving these cars two very different experiences. The M3 has a true limited-slip differential, whereas the M240i doesn’t. And yes, it’s pretty, too. On the other hand, there’s ownership experience. Things will break often and sometimes expensively on the M3. The M240i…not so much.

The M240i brings a different set of skills. It offers modern amenities that are actually useful, like Apple CarPlay and keyless entry. It’s easier to drive, too, and more enjoyable to shift—the F22 uses the delightful ZF manual, rather than the listless Getrag found in the M3. What’s more, you aren’t terribly likely to find trim pieces or headliner bits falling into your morning coffee.

item.title: A MINI Shouldn’t Survive A Trail This Rough. The Countryman Untamed Did
item.dc:creator: Horatiu Boeriu
item.description:
On the first stretch of MINI’s off-road course at Twin Peaks, a loose dirt climb above Lake Tahoe, I was already picturing the social media captions: “Even my VW Golf can do that.” Then the...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
On the first stretch of MINI’s off-road course at Twin Peaks, a loose dirt climb above Lake Tahoe, I was already picturing the social media captions: “Even my VW Golf can do that.” Then the trail turned steep, the rocks got big and the holes got bigger, and more than once I was sure the 2027 MINI Countryman Untamed was about to break something underneath. It never did.

The US unveil came right after MINI Takes the States wrapped its California weekend at Lake Tahoe, where off-road-ready vehicles are everyday transport and real trails start close to the water. MINI picked the most extreme course it could have, and I’m glad it did, because the Countryman Untamed can do far more than its marketing photos suggest. It’s a good first attempt at an off-roader MINI, and it left me convinced MINI should go much bolder with whatever comes next.

First Official “Rugged” Countryman

The Untamed is essentially an edition package for the U25 Countryman, and it’s not limited in numbers. In the US it comes on the 241-hp Countryman S ALL4 and the 308-hp electric SE ALL4, and I drove the S ALL4. Both get a 15 mm (0.6-inch) lift that adds up to 0.75 inches of ground clearance (8.75 inches on the S ALL4, 8.15 on the SE), 245/45 R19 Pirelli Scorpion All Terrain Plus tires developed for this edition, and a factory hitch rated for 3,500 pounds as standard.

The lift comes from longer dampers on the standard springs, with one non-adjustable setting. MINI says it improves approach and breakover angles, but it hasn’t published the numbers. The Experience Modes are unchanged, and the software work is in the ABS, DSC and steering, recalibrated for the height and tires.

North America is the only region where every Untamed gets ALL4, the lift and the tires. The UK fits the lift only to the SE, and mainland Europe only to the electric E and SE ALL4. The S ALL4 Untamed starts at $43,900 before destination ($45,250 with it), and MINI hasn’t priced the SE yet. UK prices run from £33,595 for the front-drive C to £40,775 for the SE, just £250 more than the S, and in Germany the package adds €4,700. Production starts at Plant Leipzig in November, and the first cars should reach US dealers around January.

Dealers will also sell the Medium AUTOHOME roof tent for about $5,000. According to the product page on their website, their roof tents have a fiberglass shell and unfold and fold in seconds thanks to two gas springs. It also seems to be enough for two adults and a child, with a mattress included. I climbed up to see if a 6″3 man could fit in there and the height was not an issue.

But it also uses most of the roof’s 165-pound driving limit (661 pounds parked), and closed it adds about 12 inches of height, so check your garage first. MINI has also teamed up with HELINOX on folding camp chairs and tables in Untamed styling.

Beyond the lift and tires, the Untamed is a styling job: a new grille with angular vertical inserts, Dark Steel trim and front and rear underbody guards, new sills and a rear diffuser, and textured matte film on the arches, sills and hood to fend off stone chips. The five-spoke wheels mimic old-school steelies, a mountain logo finally gives the oversized C-pillar something to do, and Frozen Nomad Blue is MINI’s first series-production matte paint. It joins Nomad Blue and Hideaway Grey as colors exclusive to the Untamed. Inside, knit fabrics patterned after rock formations cover the seats, dash and doors.

How The Untamed Handled A Steep, Rocky Trail At Twin Peaks

That opening dirt climb was a good test of traction on slippery surfaces. I floored it several times on the way up, and the traction was always there as long as I didn’t let the speed drop too much. I can’t think of another MINI that finds this much grip on loose dirt, and the quick steering made it easy to place the car as the surface kept changing. Where a road calibration would cut power at the first slip and kill momentum, MINI’s retune lets ALL4 and the traction control keep these tires digging in.

Then it got steep and aggressive, with big rocks, granite slabs, huge holes and little room to maneuver around them. The Countryman Untamed managed it anyway, even with drivers like me who don’t have much off-road experience.

On terrain like this the car often hangs one wheel in the air, and with no low-range gearbox or locking differentials, it relies on that retuned traction control to keep moving. Three-quarters of an inch doesn’t sound like much, but it got the nose over a few approaches I’d have hesitated to try in a regular Countryman.

There were a few spots where we felt this was it, something underneath would break. The skid plates front and rear are plastic and only lightly reworked, and the bottom of the front bumper is the first thing to touch on steep approaches, so this is where MINI has the most room to improve. Also, keep in mind that you will accept some risk of damage on a course like this.

Coming back down, the terrain went from rocks and holes back to slippery sand and dirt, and the car kept finding enough grip to inspire confidence. It was fun too, with the tail swinging out a bit whenever I floored it on the loose stuff and it was a lot of fun.

Could it do even more on bigger tires? Commenters on social media think so, and they have a point: a 245/45 R19 has only about 4.3 inches of sidewall to soak up rocks, and a taller tire would add clearance too. MINI says these Pirellis are the best balance between off-road ability and on-road comfort. A bigger lift was out too, since MINI says the taller nose would clash with European pedestrian-protection rules.

Is The Countryman Untamed Livable On The Road?

The drive back to the hotel, over smooth and rough pavement, tested the suspension. The ride was adequate for a short drive, but you feel the stiffer setup without a doubt, and it isn’t as comfortable as a regular Countryman. The taller stance and chunkier tread also bring a little more lean in corners and a softer turn-in. The cabin is louder as well, though never intrusive, and I’ll measure the difference with a decibel test during a longer drive.

The upside of the tire profile is that you feel a lot through the steering wheel, on and off road. For me it’s an easy trade, because I love the look of off-road cars and can live with a little extra noise to have one.

Overall, the Countryman Untamed delivers off-road, and the American car, with ALL4, the lift, the tires and the hitch standard, is the version that does it best. The hardware is modest and the design mostly skin-deep, so MINI has plenty of room to go further, starting with metal skid plates and taller tires. The Golf joke didn’t survive Twin Peaks, and I’m hoping the Untamed is just the beginning.

item.title: Porsche’s Electric Sports Car Arrives Soon, But BMW Has No Rival
item.dc:creator: Adrian Padeanu
item.description:
Against all odds, Porsche is moving ahead with its electric sports car plans, even as the German automaker reassesses its broader electrification strategy. The 718 EV is scheduled to enter production in 2027, and Zuffenhausen...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
Against all odds, Porsche is moving ahead with its electric sports car plans, even as the German automaker reassesses its broader electrification strategy. The 718 EV is scheduled to enter production in 2027, and Zuffenhausen is confident the two-door models can deliver the driving experience the brand is known for. BMW, meanwhile, has not yet announced a direct rival.

Although rumors have circulated that Porsche might cancel the electric Boxster and Cayman, the cars are still very much happening. CEO Michael Leiters wasn’t initially sold on the idea, though. Speaking to the media at the company’s Capital Markets Day this week, he admitted he “was very, very skeptical about this vehicle” upon his arrival as CEO in January. His doubts disappeared, however, after he got behind the wheel for the first time.

Porsche knows that putting batteries into a lightweight sports car involves more than simply replacing an engine with electric motors. The company needs to preserve the balanced handling and engaging driving dynamics that have defined the Boxster and Cayman for decades. While I was digging through investor documentation, I stumbled upon the promise of an “innovative battery concept” designed to give the 718 EVs a “mid-engine character,” even without a flat-six behind the seats.

Porsche Will Put The Battery Where The Gas Engine Used To Be

Porsche achieves this by mounting the battery where the combustion engine used to sit. Automotive News (subscription required) quotes Robert Meier, Porsche’s vice president of vehicle architecture and characteristics, explaining that the battery won’t sit in the floor, as it does in virtually all EVs. Instead, the pack occupies the space traditionally reserved for the engine, with three modules arranged across two levels. The layout delivers a 44.8:55.2 front-to-rear weight distribution. Porsche says its E-Core Architecture also lowers the center of gravity to sharpen handling.

By keeping the battery out of the floor beneath the occupants, Porsche can also lower the Boxster and Cayman’s seating position. The automaker goes as far as to say the next-generation 718 will deliver an “authentic sports car feeling thanks to low seating position.”

Expect the electric 718 to launch next year, with 2028 marking its first full year of production. Plans to bring back the Boxster and Cayman with combustion engines have been scrapped, leaving both models electric-only. Meanwhile, the 911 will continue to fill the combustion-engine role in Porsche’s sports car lineup. CEO Michael Leiters has made that distinction crystal clear, promising that the iconic coupe will never go fully electric.

Up next

  • The Electric M3 Will Be BMW’s First EV To Lose The “i”

    BMW has finally put an end to the naming speculation surrounding its first full-fat electric M car. Despite its close relationship...

  • BMW Gives Us Our Best Look Yet At The Electric M3

    With its 2027 debut drawing closer, BMW has released new teaser images showing the ZA0 prototype with its most revealing disguise...

Weight Is The Enemy Of Performance

The elephant in the room is weight. Porsche can relocate the battery to preserve the 718’s mid-engine character, but that doesn’t make the weight penalty of going electric magically disappear. It’s unclear how Zuffenhausen plans to keep the Boxster and Cayman light enough to deliver the agility expected of a sports car without resorting to extensive carbon-fiber construction, which would push prices even higher.

A smaller battery could help trim some kilos, but that would come at the expense of range. Porsche will have to strike a delicate balance between weight, driving dynamics, and efficiency, and it remains to be seen how well the engineers can pull it off.

BMW Has No Direct Rival In Sight

While Porsche is committing to electric two-door sports cars below the 911, BMW has not yet confirmed plans for a comparable model. Munich is investing heavily in EVs, including the Neue Klasse platform and a next-generation electric M3, but its announced products don’t directly challenge the 718 Boxster and Cayman.

That’s a notable gap for a company with a long history of building driver-focused coupes and roadsters. BMW’s Neue Klasse electric offensive centers on sedans and SUVs, with an i3 Touring coming in 2027. There’s also an entry-level compact model for Europe, potentially called the i1, expected to broaden the lineup when it arrives in 2028. A dedicated battery-powered sports car, however, remains unconfirmed.

Spy shots of what could be an electric i4 Convertible have offered some hope that BMW might eventually enter the two-door EV segment. However, even if that model reaches production, BMW has yet to indicate plans to make it a direct rival to Porsche’s mid-engine sports cars. An electric i4 Coupe seems like an educated guess, but M Performance and full-fat M versions are likely still a long way off.

BMW could still surprise us, but for now, Porsche is taking the risk on electric sports cars while its Bavarian rival keeps its cards close to its chest.

item.title: BMW Shows Off The New iX4 In Walkaround Video
item.dc:creator: Adrian Padeanu
item.description:
BMW has a new walkaround video, and the star of the show is the iX4. The electric SUV with a sloping roofline recently broke cover, but there’s always room to take another look at a...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
BMW has a new walkaround video, and the star of the show is the iX4. The electric SUV with a sloping roofline recently broke cover, but there’s always room to take another look at a new model, especially one that modernizes the coupe-SUV formula in a Neue Klasse package. The video also features the iX3 M60, giving us the first chance to see the two Debrecen-built EVs together.

As expected, the iX4 looks a lot like the iX3 from the front. That’s hardly surprising, given they share the same design DNA. The big difference appears toward the rear, where the roofline slopes down, giving the iX4 a sportier profile. It’s the usual trade-off: a little less practicality in exchange for a more stylish shape.

Whether that compromise is worth it is up to you. Some people will prefer the conventional iX3, while others will happily sacrifice a bit of headroom and cargo space for a more rakish design. BMW knows there’s a market for both, which explains why it didn’t stop at one electric SUV. The arguably cooler-looking iX4 comes with a couple of standard features its more conventional sibling doesn’t get: the M Sport Package and a panoramic glass roof. Of course, you can add both to the iX3 by ticking a couple of boxes on the options list.

The iX3 M60 Makes A Special Appearance

The walkaround doesn’t focus exclusively on the iX4. BMW also gives us a look at the iX3 M60 xDrive, which packs the same 603 hp planned for the future iX4 M60. With 875 Nm (645 lb-ft) of torque sent to both axles, the electric SUV can sprint from 0 to 100 km/h (62 mph) in just 3.9 seconds. The M Performance version also gets adaptive M suspension, variable sport steering, and an M Sport differential. In other words, it’s not just about adding more power and calling it a day.

Still, the iX3 M60 takes a back seat here. The iX4 is the newer face in BMW’s electric lineup, and this video gives us another opportunity to check out the coupe-SUV before it reaches dealerships in the coming months.

BMW has spent years convincing buyers that an SUV doesn’t have to look like a box on wheels. Now it’s applying that same idea to electric vehicles. Whether the iX4 makes more sense than the iX3 is debatable, but at least buyers will have a choice. That’s never a bad thing, right?

item.title: BMW Asked Americans How Much EV Range They Need. The Answer Is Surprising
item.dc:creator: Adrian Padeanu
item.description:
Americans want electric cars that can travel hundreds of miles on a charge, even though most don’t really need nearly that much range for their daily commute. That’s one of the key findings from a...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
Americans want electric cars that can travel hundreds of miles on a charge, even though most don’t really need nearly that much range for their daily commute. That’s one of the key findings from a new BMW survey, which suggests range anxiety remains a major concern for potential EV buyers despite advances in battery technology.

The automaker asked Big Village to conduct an online survey of 1,005 U.S. adults last month to understand their attitudes toward electric vehicles. The results paint an interesting picture: 73% of respondents said 75 miles or less would be enough for their daily driving, yet 42% want at least 300 miles of range before considering an EV. More specifically, 18% said they’d want 400 miles or more.

In other words, what drivers think they need and what they want from an electric car are two different things. Range also remains a deciding factor for 72% of respondents when shopping for an EV, suggesting that buyers still place considerable importance on the freedom to travel farther than their usual routines demand.

Americans Want Faster Charging, Too

BMW’s survey suggests faster charging could help close the gap between expectations and everyday driving needs. Some 53% of respondents said they’d be more likely to consider an EV if it could add approximately 150 miles of range in just 10 minutes at a fast-charging station.

That figure rose to 70% among Gen Z respondents and 65% among Millennials, compared with 52% among Gen X and 30% among Baby Boomers. Younger drivers appear particularly interested in reducing charging stops to just a few minutes rather than spending half an hour or longer plugged in.

Charging-time expectations are also becoming more flexible. According to the survey, 55% of Americans now consider 30 minutes or less an acceptable charging time, up from 48% in 2025. Meanwhile, 76% said they’d accept a charging stop of up to an hour, compared with 71% last year.

BMW is already exceeding those expectations with the new iX3. At an 800-volt DC fast-charging station, the electric SUV can add an estimated 185 miles of range in 10 minutes, surpassing the 150-mile benchmark that would make an EV more appealing to many respondents.

Price Remains The Biggest Obstacle To EV Adoption

Range isn’t the only thing keeping American drivers from electric mobility. Upfront purchase price was the most frequently cited barrier to EV ownership, with 51% of respondents pointing to cost.

Battery longevity and replacement costs came next at 31%, followed by charging time at 26%. Driving range and public charging availability each concerned 24% of respondents, while 23% cited a lack of convenient home-charging access.

Interestingly, 27% of Americans said lower ownership and operating costs would encourage them to consider an EV. Performance, advanced technology, and environmental benefits each attracted 19% of respondents. That suggests electric cars appeal for more than just their potential to reduce emissions, although the initial purchase price remains a major hurdle.

The used-car market could help. Some 55% of respondents said they’d consider a certified pre-owned or used electric vehicle if the savings were substantial enough.

Despite these hurdles, BMW found that 68% of Americans would consider buying an electric vehicle. Only 56% now view EV buyers as early adopters, down from 62% in 2025. That shift suggests electric cars are gradually becoming a more familiar option rather than a niche choice for technology enthusiasts.

There’s also a growing appreciation for performance. Some 38% of respondents believe EVs accelerate faster than comparable gasoline-powered cars, a perception shared by 47% of Gen Z and 49% of Millennials. Among Baby Boomers, that figure drops to 25%.

Up next

  • 2026 BMW iX3 EPA Range: How Wheel Choice Affects Your Miles

    Pick the wrong tires on the 2026 BMW iX3 and you’re leaving 51 miles of EPA range on the table — before you’ve e...

  • The New BMW i7 M70 Brings Even More Power And Extra Range

    Our deep dive into the 2027 BMW 7 Series continues with the i7 M70. The electric M Performance version has also received updates t...

What Are People Doing When The EV’s Battery Is Charging?

BMW also asked what people might do during a 20- to 30-minute public charging stop. Calling or texting friends and family topped the list at 43%, followed by grabbing coffee or something to eat at 41%. Another 36% would relax or read, while 29% would stream entertainment or play a game.

More importantly, 57% said they’d be more likely to consider an EV if it could supply backup electricity to their home during a power outage. BMW’s new iX3 supports bidirectional charging, including Vehicle-to-Home functionality, when paired with suitable home-charging equipment.

Of course, a survey commissioned by an automaker with a growing electric lineup should be viewed in context. Still, the findings highlight a familiar industry challenge: convincing buyers that an EV fits their lifestyle while making the technology affordable and convenient.

BMW’s own products are moving in that direction. The Spartanburg-made electric iX5 is expected to deliver up to 435 miles of EPA-estimated range in the United States, while the iX3 demonstrates how quickly charging technology is advancing. The electric i3 sedan and the recently revealed iX4 are also on the way. Hopefully, Americans will also get the i3 Touring when it launches in 2027, though we’ve heard it might not get a US visa after all.

The irony is that most Americans surveyed don’t need anything close to 300 miles for their daily driving. But buying a car isn’t just about the commute. People want the freedom to take a spontaneous road trip without planning every stop around a charger. Until charging infrastructure, charging speeds, and prices make that flexibility feel effortless, automakers will have to keep giving customers the range figures they want, even when their daily routines suggest they could get by with considerably less.

Who knew Americans would be so demanding, right?

item.title: The New iX3 M60 All But Confirms The i3 M60’s 603 hp. Here’s What Else We Know About The Sedan
item.dc:creator: Horatiu Boeriu
item.description:
BMW still won’t say how much power the i3 M60 xDrive makes, but the iX3 M60 xDrive it revealed this week makes the answer easy to guess. The electric SUV gets 450 kW (603 hp)...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
BMW still won’t say how much power the i3 M60 xDrive makes, but the iX3 M60 xDrive it revealed this week makes the answer easy to guess. The electric SUV gets 450 kW (603 hp) from a dual-motor Gen6 M eDrive setup. That matches the figure we were already hearing for the sedan, and it would put the i3 M60 roughly 140 hp above the i3 50 xDrive, currently the strongest version of the Neue Klasse i3 (NA0).

When BMW confirmed the M60 sedan last month, it called the car “ultra-potent” and left out output, acceleration, and price. For reference, the i3 50 xDrive makes 345 kW (463 hp) and 645 Nm (476 lb-ft), enough for 0-100 km/h (0-62 mph) in 4.7 seconds. The gas-powered M350 xDrive makes 437 hp in US spec, so a 603-hp i3 M60 would be the most powerful car in the new 3 Series lineup until the electric M3 arrives.

Will The i3 M60 Share The iX3 M60’s Drivetrain?

Everything BMW has said so far points that way. Both cars use two Gen6 M eDrive motors, one per axle, run by the Heart of Joy computer and BMW M Dynamic Performance Control. Both get steering-wheel paddles that change how the M eDrive system responds, and both are due to start production in the first half of 2027. In the iX3 M60, the rear motor gets a new stator and a 420-amp inverter, up from 300 amps, and there’s no reason to expect the sedan to get different hardware.

If it does share that hardware, the i3 M60 should also inherit the SUV’s 875 Nm (645 lb-ft) of torque. The iX3 M60 does 0-100 km/h in 3.9 seconds, and the lower sedan, which should also weigh less, ought to beat that.

How Does 603 hp Compare To The i4 M60 And Electric M3?

Next to BMW’s older electric M Performance cars, the number is less dramatic. The i4 M60 xDrive makes 442 kW (593 hp) with Boost engaged, so a 450-kW i3 M60 would add just 8 kW, or about 10 hp. It’s also below the 620 to 630 hp we expected when we previewed the car a year ago. The gap to the top of the range looks deliberate, though. The first electric M3 (ZA0) is due in 2027 with four motors, one per wheel, and we expect it to make around 800 hp.

Range is where the i3 M60 should pull clear. The iX3 M60 uses the same 108.7-kWh battery as the 50 xDrive models and is rated at up to 754 km (468 miles) WLTP. That makes a figure of up to 830 km (516 miles) sound reasonable. The i4 M60 manages 551 km (342 miles).

What Else BMW Has Confirmed About The i3 M60

Inside, BMW lists M Sport seats with 10-way electric adjustment and a massage function. Outside, the M60 gets its own front light graphic, M-specific taillights, and the M Yellow Lights it shares with the M350 xDrive and the iX3 M60. There are also 21-inch Style 1067M aero wheels and red brake calipers. BMW’s M Performance Parts for the car include a carbon fiber rear spoiler raised off the trunk lid with two large cutouts, a matching front lip, carbon winglets, and a rear diffuser.

When Does The i3 M60 Arrive In The US, And What Will It Cost?

BMW of North America says i3 M60 production starts in early 2027. The iX3 M60 follows a similar schedule, with orders opening at the end of January and production starting in Debrecen, Hungary, next spring. Neither car has a price yet. The i3 50 xDrive starts at $61,500 before destination ($62,850 with the $1,350 fee), and the M60 should land well above that.

item.title: BMW’s Best Red Paint Colors of All Time, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Steven Paul
item.description:
Every time we assemble one of these “best BMW colors” compendiums, I start out with a handful of excellent colors that need to be included. Among them, inevitably, is at least two shades of red—which...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
Every time we assemble one of these “best BMW colors” compendiums, I start out with a handful of excellent colors that need to be included. Among them, inevitably, is at least two shades of red—which you’ll read a little bit about in a minute. With zero variation, every time, I end up bumping the reds for a slightly more iconic, or slightly subtler color. In the end, we often end up with no reds on the list at all. Which is a shame, and a disservice to some of the best colors in BMW’s arsenal. It’s red’s time to shine, and here are the five best BMW ever splashed metal with.

Cinnabar Red

Cinnabar Red appears on one of the most iconic BMWs ever: the E30 M3. It’s such an important color that it was deemed legendary enough to include on BMW’s Edition 50 Jahre M3. Not surprising to see this color featured alongside legendary shades like Techno Violet and Fire Orange. It also appears on Ronnie Fieg’s KITH’d out E30, too. Cinnabar is the “safest” color on this list and also one of my favorites because of it. It isn’t too bright or orangey, which makes it a great true red. It only helps matters that it appears on a truly iconic vehicle.

Vegas Red Metallic

Vegas Red is by far the newest color on the list, but it’s well deserved. Vegas Red appears all over the current BMW lineup, and arguably one of its best applications is on the vaunted G87 M2. You also catch Vegas Red on other models like the X3, 3 Series, and X1. You may also know it as Fire Red in markets outside the United States. It’s a darker metallic true red, and you’ll likely experience it differently depending on the light you’re standing in. Vegas Red debuted in 2023 on the X2 and then-new G60 5 Series before spreading throughout the lineup.

Indianapolis Red

A dark burgundy inspired by Indianapolis Motor Speedway, Indianapolis Red debuted over twenty years ago on the mighty, V10-powered E60 generation M5 and M6.  After leaving the catalog for quite a while, it returned, as BMW apparently showcased the color on the 2027 BMW X5. The deep, complex, almost brown metallic paint is a rare find, and it’s very unusual to spot the color anywhere other than the E6X generation cars. That said, it’s been an Individual option for a while, so it’ll pop up from time to time, usually on M cars. Another fantastic dark red. You can almost hear that V10 yowl just looking at it!

Aventurine Red

I know.  I clearly have a thing for dark reds, but this is the last one, I promise. Aventurine (sometimes Aventurin) Red debuted on the G15 8 Series, although we’ve seen it elsewhere on the M3 and even the 7 Series. Today Aventurine Red is still available on the M3 as a great alternative to the slightly orangey and less-saturated Toronto Red. It’s another dark red; think of it as a marginally brighter and less brown version of Indianapolis. It’s also part of BMW’s Individual palette, so you can order it on a whole mess of different cars. For the right price, that is.

Imola Red

Imola has somehow eluded every paint countdown I’ve done with BMWBLOG, and it’s a crying shame. But not today. Just slightly darker than Cinnabar to my eye, Imola has appeared on almost every great BMW from the “golden era.” We’re talking E46 M3, E39 M5, the pictured X5 4.8is, and even a small number of E36 M3s. I personally shopped for an Imola Red M Coupe before finding my current Boston Green car. Which kind of makes sense when you consider the E36 generation saw the color’s initial debut.

Likely part of Imola Red’s allure comes exactly from the color’s presence on those aforementioned legendary cars. But it’s also just a great looking red; bright, but not orange, and deep enough to be compelling. It’s the best red in the business, and BMW’s got no shortage of alternatives. Do you think Imola deserves the top spot?

item.title: This BMW iX3’s Red-Over-White Spec Is Seriously Bold
item.dc:creator: Adrian Padeanu
item.description:
Even though BMW finally revealed the iX4 this week, it doesn’t mean we’re suddenly going to stop talking about the car that kicked off the Neue Klasse product offensive. Yes, we’re bringing the iX3 back...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
Even though BMW finally revealed the iX4 this week, it doesn’t mean we’re suddenly going to stop talking about the car that kicked off the Neue Klasse product offensive. Yes, we’re bringing the iX3 back into the limelight with a fresh photo gallery featuring a 50 xDrive. Sure, it may not be as exciting as the M60, but it still has plenty going for it.

For starters, this is one of the most eye-catching iX3 builds we’ve seen so far. The electric SUV wears Fire Red paint, which already gives it plenty of visual presence, but BMW didn’t stop there. The flashy exterior is paired with 22-inch Individual wheels that add even more drama to the new-era EV. With its extended black accents, the M Sport Pro Package takes the exterior up another notch.

Things get even more interesting once you open the door. This particular iX3 has a Digital White interior that continues the bold theme from the outside. Even the steering wheel gets the white treatment as an Individual upgrade, making this about as far removed from the usual black-on-black BMW spec as you can get.

No Expense Spared

We have this particular car’s build sheet, and it reveals a long list of optional goodies. In other words, this isn’t simply an iX3 that happened to get an attention-grabbing paint job. Someone went deep into the configurator and checked quite a few boxes. The options list also includes goodies that make the cabin more pleasant, including a panoramic glass roof that comes standard on the iX4 we mentioned earlier.

Other extras tacked onto this no-expense-spared build include three-zone automatic climate control and BMW’s next-generation 3D head-up display. Honorable mentions also go to the Harman Kardon surround-sound system, heated steering wheel, retractable tow bar, and Parking Assistant Professional. Factor in a few more miscellaneous items, and this iX3 50 xDrive carries nearly €20,000 worth of options in Slovakia.

It’s especially true when you get carried away ticking boxes on the options list. We’d be glad to be in such a privileged position, even if it’s for a press car like this one.

item.title: The BMW iX4 Is Already On The Assembly Line In Hungary. Here Are The First Photos From The Plant
item.dc:creator: Horatiu Boeriu
item.description:
BMW has released the first photos of the BMW iX4 (NA7) being built at its Debrecen plant in Hungary, a day after the electric coupe-SUV’s world premiere. That makes the iX4 the second Neue Klasse...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
BMW has released the first photos of the BMW iX4 (NA7) being built at its Debrecen plant in Hungary, a day after the electric coupe-SUV’s world premiere. That makes the iX4 the second Neue Klasse model to come out of Debrecen, a factory that only started series production of the iX3 in late October 2025.

The iX4 arrives at a plant with no spare hours left. Debrecen has spent its first year chasing iX3 orders: BMW brought the second shift forward in early 2026, only a few months into production, and switched to a three-shift pattern in September so the line now runs 24 hours a day, and the iX4 has to fit into that schedule.

BMW hasn’t said how it will split Debrecen’s output between the two models, or whether iX3 delivery times will stretch once the iX4 ramps up. The iX4 does have one thing going for it: it shares its platform and Gen6 drivetrain hardware with the iX3, so it should slot onto the existing lines more easily than a car built on different underpinnings. Shared parts don’t add hours to the day, though, and Debrecen is already using all 24 of them.

When Does The iX4 Go On Sale, And How Much Does It Cost?

The iX4 40 xDrive and 50 xDrive go on sale in March 2027. In the US, the iX4 50 xDrive starts at $66,200 before destination. In Germany, the range opens at €70,900 for the iX4 40 xDrive, €5,000 more than the equivalent iX3. The iX4 M60 xDrive enters production in March 2027 and reaches showrooms later in the year.

Underneath, the iX4 is an iX3 with a lower, sloping roof, and that roofline pays off on paper: its drag coefficient is 0.23, against the iX3’s 0.24. Here’s how the three versions compare, with BMW’s provisional WLTP range figures:

  • iX4 40 xDrive: 275 kW (369 hp), 520 Nm (384 lb-ft), 0-100 km/h (0-62 mph) in 5.6 seconds, up to 638 km (396 miles)
  • iX4 50 xDrive: 345 kW (463 hp), 645 Nm (476 lb-ft), 0-100 km/h in 4.9 seconds, up to 828 km (514 miles)
  • iX4 M60 xDrive: 450 kW (603 hp), 875 Nm (645 lb-ft), 0-100 km/h in 3.9 seconds, up to 777 km (483 miles)

The 50 xDrive’s 828 km is 22 km more than the iX3 50 xDrive’s WLTP rating, so the coupe roof costs nothing in range and buys a little back. It does cost some luggage space: the iX4 holds 490 liters behind the rear seats, 30 liters less than the iX3. DC fast charging peaks at 400 kW on the 50 xDrive and M60, and 300 kW on the 40 xDrive. US range figures will come in lower than the WLTP numbers once the EPA rates the car.

The First BMW X4 That Won’t Come From South Carolina

Both previous X4 generations, the F26 and the G02, were built in Spartanburg, South Carolina. As we reported in July, BMW has no plans to build the electric X4 in Spartanburg or at its San Luis Potosí plant in Mexico, so, for now at least, every US-market iX4 will be shipped from Europe.

Debrecen covers more than 400 hectares (about 990 acres) and cost BMW roughly €2 billion. It’s built around the company’s iFactory approach, with heavy automation and digital planning, and it assembles Gen6 high-voltage batteries on site. BMW says it’s the group’s first vehicle plant to run entirely on renewable electricity during normal operation, with rooftop solar panels supplying part of that and surplus solar energy going into a large thermal storage system.

The harder test comes in March 2027, when iX4 deliveries begin and the iX4 M60 joins the line. From then on, Debrecen will be building two body styles, each with its own M60, on the same round-the-clock schedule that iX3 demand alone forced on it this year.

item.title: MINI Countryman Untamed Shows Its Dirty Side At Athens Show
item.dc:creator: Adrian Padeanu
item.description:
At least compared to other MINIs, the Countryman has been a little more willing to leave the pavement. Now, the new Untamed Edition is taking that idea seriously. Making its European premiere at the 2026...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
At least compared to other MINIs, the Countryman has been a little more willing to leave the pavement. Now, the new Untamed Edition is taking that idea seriously. Making its European premiere at the 2026 Athens Auto Show in Greece, the rugged crossover brings a handful of hardware upgrades designed to make it more convincing when the road runs out.

MINI unveiled the Countryman Untamed Edition earlier this week, and the Athens event gives visitors their first chance to see the adventure-focused variant in person. The event runs through October 11, with MINI bringing its full lineup to the Greek capital. This isn’t merely a Countryman wearing extra plastic cladding and an adventurous name.

Depending on the market and powertrain, it gets a 15-millimeter suspension lift, increasing ground clearance by up to 19 mm. The revised setup improves the approach and breakover angles, while MINI recalibrates the ABS, DSC, and steering systems to match the changes. It also rides on specially developed Pirelli Scorpion All Terrain Plus tires wrapped around unique 19-inch alloy wheels. They’re standard in North America but optional in Europe, where MINI apparently realizes that not every Countryman owner is secretly plotting an expedition into the wilderness.

Styling Tweaks Inside And Out

The extra hardware gets backed up by a redesigned grille, Dark Steel exterior accents, new underbody protection, revised side sills, and a sculpted rear diffuser. Protective textured films cover the wheel arches, side sills, and hood bulge, adding visual toughness while helping protect the body from the inevitable stones and debris encountered off smooth tarmac.

MINI offers several colors for the Untamed Edition, including Hideaway Grey, Nomad Blue, and Frozen Nomad Blue, along with Nanuq White and Midnight Black. The latter two aren’t nearly as adventurous-sounding, but at least they give buyers an escape from the blue-and-gray theme. Frozen Nomad Blue is particularly noteworthy because it’s the first matte exterior finish MINI has offered for series production.

Inside, the outdoor theme continues with Vescin Nightshade Blue sports seats featuring knitted sections inspired by rock formations. Cornflower Blue stitching and accents add a splash of color, while the dashboard and door panels feature a knitted Millennial Melange surface. Even the center-console storage box borrows cues from outdoor equipment, with elastic retaining straps that look like they belong on a backpack rather than a crossover.

Up next

  • MINI Countryman Untamed Edition Debuts With Off-Road Attitude

    MINI is taking the Countryman somewhere it probably doesn’t spend much time: off the pavement. Say hello to the new Untamed...

  • MINI’s Toughest Countryman Yet Takes On The 2026 Rebelle Rally

    BMW has been a regular at the Rebelle Rally in recent years, entering everything from the X2 to the X5. Now, it’s MINI’s turn. For...

Gone Camping

And because no modern adventure vehicle is complete without somewhere to sleep, MINI has teamed up with Italian specialist AUTOHOME for a roof tent. It opens in seconds and features weather-resistant materials, panoramic openings, and fiberglass-reinforced construction. There’s also a camping collection developed with HELINOX, including folding chairs and tables.

Power comes in multiple flavors depending on the market. The Untamed Edition will be available with the Countryman C, Countryman D, and Countryman S ALL4, as well as the electric Countryman E and SE ALL4. The all-wheel-drive versions obviously make the most sense for buyers planning to venture farther from civilization. We’re actually surprised MINI even offers this version with front-wheel drive.

European production will begin in November at BMW Group Plant Leipzig, with the market launch scheduled for early 2027.

So, while the Countryman Untamed Edition isn’t about turning the MINI into a hardcore off-roader, it does give the brand’s largest model a little more credibility when the pavement disappears. The extra clearance, all-terrain tires, and ALL4 make this more than just another lifestyle special.

item.title: This Mall Has Everything From 1930s BMWs To The New i3
item.dc:creator: Adrian Padeanu
item.description:
If you want to see how far BMW has come over roughly a century of making cars and motorcycles, a Prague shopping mall has the answer. The brand has squeezed everything from rare prewar machines...

First published by https://www.bmwblog.com
item.content:encoded:
If you want to see how far BMW has come over roughly a century of making cars and motorcycles, a Prague shopping mall has the answer. The brand has squeezed everything from rare prewar machines to modern M cars and motorcycles into one exhibition at OC Arkády. And now, there’s a rather important new arrival: the i3.

The exhibition, organized with BMW dealer CarTec Praha, runs through October 15, so you have a week left as of this writing. You can visit the display for free during the shopping center’s opening hours. Putting the new i3 in a collection of historic cars is actually a pretty clever move. After all, the latest electric sedan shows where BMW is going, while the cars around it show where the company has been.

The second-generation i3 (well, third if you’re counting the China-only sedan) is the newest addition to the exhibition. It gets plenty of attention as the second Neue Klasse model after the iX3. In Czech-spec form, BMW quotes a range of up to 912 kilometers (567 miles), which is quite the flex for a car sitting among machines never particularly concerned with how far they could travel between charging stops.

From i3 To Pre-War Cars

The new i3 is also an important car for BMW beyond its impressive range figure. Styling-wise, it’s essentially the electric counterpart to the new G50 3 Series, sharing much of the same Neue Klasse aesthetic. Inside, the two also look like they’re cut from the same cloth, despite being fundamentally different cars underneath.

Of course, the exhibition’s point is to remind visitors that BMW didn’t start yesterday. The display includes rare historic cars, including the 328, 335, 326, 315, 319, Z1, and even an Isetta. There’s also a particularly rare 335 convertible wearing bodywork from Swiss coachbuilder Graber. Only two were built, making it a car that probably deserves its own security detail.

Up next

  • The 2027 BMW i3 40 xDrive Is A New Entry-Level Model

    BMW is expanding the i3 lineup with a cheaper version that trades some performance for a smaller battery and a lower price. Meet t...

  • BMW i3 M60 xDrive Officially Announced, Coming In 2027

    It was only a matter of time before BMW announced it would give the new i3 the M Performance treatment. Next year, the fully elect...

An Eclectic BMW Lineup At The Mall

The exhibition also celebrates the 40th anniversary of the original E30 M3, which feels appropriate given that BMW’s M division has spent decades turning relatively sensible cars into relatively irresponsible ones. Sticking to the M side, the M2 is also on the lineup. On the electric side, the i3 is joined by its crossover twin, the iX3.

The motorcycle side is just as ambitious. Motorrad is showing everything from prewar machines such as the R42, R2, and R61 to modern performance bikes. Highlights include the M 1000 RR Toprak Edition, R 12 Toprak Passion, and an M 1000 RR TT edition inspired by the legendary Isle of Man Tourist Trophy. Other bikes include the R 1300 R, R 1300 GS Adventure, F 450 GS, R 18 Bobber, F 900 R, and S 1000 XR. Czech news portal iDNES has a massive photo gallery spanning nearly a century’s worth of BMWs.

That’s arguably what makes the exhibition more interesting than a conventional new-car display. You can walk past a prewar BMW, an E30 M3-era icon, an M2, a motorcycle, and then arrive at a Neue Klasse EV. It’s essentially a century of BMW history condensed into one shopping-mall visit.

item.content:encoded:
Like clockwork, BMW has already fired up the German configurator for the iX4. Screenshots from the online build tool show what €70,900 buys you, provided you stay away from the options list. Compared with its traditionally shaped sibling, the iX3, its cooler cousin has a couple of aces up its sleeve. And no, we’re not talking about that roofline we’re hoping to see one day on an actual coupe.

We are talking about the M Sport Package, which comes standard on the iX4. Similarly, even the base model gets the panoramic glass roof. These two additions to the standard equipment instantly elevate the coupe-ified SUV’s appearance, even if the body color is underwhelming. No surprise there, with Alpine White being the only finish that doesn’t command a premium.

You know times have changed when even the base configuration gets 20-inch wheels. We’re not talking about a 7 Series, but a crossover positioned in the 3 Series/X3 segment. Predictably, they don’t look nearly as exciting as the wheels BMW showcased in the official release, but for a zero-option model, they’re not too shabby either.

Which To Choose: iX3 Or iX4?

Of course, “zero-option” is debatable because you get some goodies the iX3 doesn’t have from the start. The iX4 40 xDrive costs a full €5,000 more than an iX3 40 xDrive. Add the M Sport Package, and the difference shrinks to just €1,200. In fact, adding the panoramic glass roof makes the iX3 a little more expensive. That’s not to say the iX4 is suddenly the better deal, as some buyers will naturally prioritize practicality over style, opting for the bigger cargo area and increased rear headroom.

But the iX4 40 xDrive has a slight advantage in range. It goes 638 kilometers (396 miles) on a single charge in the WLTP cycle, or 17 km (nearly 11 miles) more than the iX3 40 xDrive. The difference stems from the iX4’s more aero-friendly shape and slightly lower drag coefficient. Similarly, the iX4 50 xDrive has a minor range advantage over its iX3 equivalent, with 828 km (515 miles) versus 806 km (501 miles).

The BMW iX4 M60 Will Arrive In The Configurator In Late January 2027

These are the only two versions available to configure in Germany for now. A third flavor will join them at the end of January 2027, when BMW adds the iX4 M60. Don’t hold your breath for another X4 with combustion engines, because the company has made it crystal clear that the ICE has handed over the baton to the EV.

We’ll be doing the exact opposite of this configurator exercise by loading up the iX4 with options to the brim, so watch this space. However, we won’t know how much a fully optioned “NA7” really costs until the M Performance version arrives, and whether we can push it into six-figure territory as we recently did with the new 3 Series.
